summary: Comprehensive backend test suite (34 tests) for the re-engagement email nudge system. 33/34 pass. One legitimate business-logic bug found: the scheduler's recency gate (skipped_recent) checks the absolute most-recent nudge for the user and does NOT respect the nudge_sequence_reset_at watermark, so a user who logs in and then goes stale again is blocked from receiving a fresh 72h nudge until 72h have elapsed since the OLD nudge — instead of firing right away because the old nudge is 'water under the bridge' per the spec.

critical.issue: The recency check (server.py ~line 741-749) uses the last email_nudges doc for the user without filtering by sent_at > nudge_sequence_reset_at. Consequence: after a user logs in (resets watermark) and then goes stale, the tick still counts a pre-reset nudge as 'recent' and skips them. Fix: change last query to {'user_id': u['id'], 'sent_at': {'$gt': reset_at}} so recency is scoped to post-reset nudges only, mirroring how the already-sent check at line 764 handles the watermark.

action_items: In server.py _reengagement_tick(), scope the recency gate to nudges sent after nudge_sequence_reset_at (or last_login_at as fallback). Currently line ~741: `last = await db.email_nudges.find_one({"user_id": u["id"]}, sort=[("sent_at", -1)])` — should be `find_one({"user_id": u["id"], **({"sent_at": {"$gt": reset_at}} if reset_at else {})}, sort=[("sent_at", -1)])`. But note reset_at is computed later in the function; move that computation up, or duplicate. This makes the login-reset test pass and matches the product spec 'reset sequence on login'.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 8044 lines — well past the 700-line guidance. The re-engagement module (~465-775) is a good candidate to extract into backend/reengagement.py.
In nudge_track_click (line 1653): the first update_one uses `"$setOnInsert": {}` which is a no-op since upsert isn't enabled — harmless but confusing, remove it.
Anti-open-redirect check `dest.startswith(base + '/') or dest == base` is correct but fragile — a base URL with trailing slash would break it. Consider urllib.parse comparison of netlocs instead.

In _reengagement_tick the recency gate is computed BEFORE the reset watermark is read (line 741 vs 764). Combining them or ordering them by watermark first would be cleaner and would have caught the login-reset bug.

The recency gate uses `recency_hours = 72 if cadence == 'default' else (7*24)`. For 'off' cadence users we also enter this branch but they're already filtered by the earlier nudge_unsubscribed check — OK but worth a comment.
email_nudges collection lacks an explicit unique index on `id` — the app relies on uuid4 collisions being negligible. Consider adding a unique index in _lifespan_startup.
test_credentials: admin@example.com / from backend/.env ADMIN_PASSWORD (via _creds.py). New TEST_ users created per-test and cleaned up.
seed_data_creation: All test data is prefixed TEST_ and cleaned up in each test's finally block (email_nudges + users + wellness_journey). One admin-engagement test creates 4 nudges and deletes them.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Test file at /app/backend/tests/test_reengagement_nudges.py is designed to run with `-n 0` because it uses a session-scoped asyncio event loop and rebinds server.db to that loop (to avoid Motor 'Event loop is closed' when using default asyncio.run per-test). It requires MongoDB access via pymongo (same MONGO_URL/DB_NAME as backend). Tests use unittest.mock.patch to bypass Resend (_send_email_sync + _resend + _RESEND_API_KEY) and _in_send_window_cst for full-flow tests. If _reengagement_tick is refactored, re-check the mock targets. The single failing test (test_login_reset_watermark) is a real spec-vs-impl gap — do NOT skip it; it should pass after the recency-gate fix described in action_items.
rca of the issue: test_login_reset_watermark: The tick's recency gate (server.py line ~741) finds the most recent email_nudges doc regardless of whether it was sent before the user's login-reset watermark. After the login (which sets nudge_sequence_reset_at = now), the previous nudge is only ~seconds old, so the 72h recency guard skips the user. Reproduction: (1) seed user last_login=100h ago, reset_at=100h ago; (2) run tick → nudge #1 (72h tier) inserted; (3) set last_login_at + nudge_sequence_reset_at to now; (4) rewind last_login_at only to 100h ago; (5) run tick → SHOULD send nudge #2 per spec, but the recency guard sees nudge #1 (~seconds old) and returns skipped_recent. Fix: scope the recency query to `sent_at > nudge_sequence_reset_at` (or `> last_login_at` fallback), mirroring the already-sent check further down the function.
